A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Dial-In LLM and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C. Relocated and renumbered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v3 reports original Chinese and English clustering experiments, LLM utility evaluations, downstream classification results, and ablations, including additional evaluations in Appendix C.

after.justification: v4 retains those empirical results and adds downstream comparisons, English utility evaluations, and an inter-annotator agreement study.

M1.justification: Section 3.4 corrects the written agent-role assignment rule from excluding answer-type labels to including them. This changes the stated predicate, although an implementation change is not established. The iterative clustering, naming, merging, and role-separation framework otherwise remains intact.

E1.justification: Both retain the 55,085-sentence Chinese corpus and BANK77, CLINC(I), MTOP(I), and MASSIVE(I). Additional agreement and English utility evaluations stay within existing task and language coverage. Removing OOS from descriptive Table 1 does not establish removal of an evaluated dataset.

E2.justification: The downstream BERT comparison expands from a base-model comparison to explicitly include ClusterLLM, LLMEdgeRefine, IDAS, and Keyphrase Expansion alongside K-Means in v4 Table 6. Appendix C also introduces LLaMA-2-13B and Mistral-7B alternatives in English utility comparisons. This substantially expands competitive validation, while the main clustering comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: New protocols include five experts assessing 100 K-means clusters containing 2,000 sentences under binary and 1–4 annotation schemes, and evaluation of additional LLM configurations on 100 annotated English clusters. These supplement the retained experimental settings; the main clustering metrics and stated training budgets are unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 5.6 adds a direct test of annotation reliability, while Appendix C examines English utility performance across model sizes and families. Table 15 extends sampling sensitivity results with ChatGLM random-sampling rows; much of that table redisplays the unchanged Figure 3. Existing merging, scoring, and search-pruning analyses remain.

E5.justification: v4 first reports five-seed averaging and mean±standard deviation for the main clustering results, and five-run uncertainty for English utilities. It also adds Fleiss’ kappa for annotation agreement. Tables 4 and 6 introduce significance-style asterisks without defining tests or thresholds. These are substantial reporting additions, not evidence of an explicitly increased run count.

E6.justification: Main Chinese clustering estimates and English Table 5 scores remain unchanged. v4 adds downstream accuracies of 62%, 63%, 68%, and 72% for ClusterLLM, LLMEdgeRefine, IDAS, and Keyphrase Expansion, respectively, plus 73% for context-free LLM-ITL. English utility results, agreement kappas of 0.82 versus 0.59, and additional sampling results expand the evidence substantially. Cost accounting rises from 480 to approximately 560 calls by including naming.

T1.justification: The mathematical definition of the agent-role set in Section 3.4 changes from non-membership to membership in the answer-label set, correcting a substantive predicate error. The clustering objective, hyperspherical merging equations, and other mathematical content remain unchanged; no new theorem or proof appears.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain the Chinese dataset, human-aligned coherence and naming utilities, and iterative context-aware clustering with quality, efficiency, and downstream benefits. v4 foregrounds an 18.46% relative downstream gain, but this quantifies an already claimed benefit rather than introducing a new central contribution.

C2.justification: v4 adds tentative explanations linking weaker downstream results to label noise or excessive granularity, contrasts these with IDAS’s conservative refinement, and interprets the new agreement and English model comparisons. It also specifies NMI’s bias toward larger cluster counts. The substantive limitations concerning coherence-only evaluation, language/domain coverage, and sentence-level scope are retained.

D1.justification: Appendix A adds annotator qualifications and a mandatory training session with 50 labeled clusters, whereas v3 mentions five naming examples; reannotation is not established. The data-access statement changes from an anonymized sample link and promised release to a named GitHub repository described as available, while model-release promises disappear. Section 3.3 also changes the stated merging threshold of 0.7 into an example value.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially expands positioning relative to topic modeling, information retrieval, contextual intent understanding, and data-, model-, and task-level LLM integration. Corresponding literature is added, including Allahyari et al., Carberry and Flowers, several Jiang works, and Qu et al.; the Haodi Zhang et al. crowdsourcing citation is removed. This exceeds bibliographic maintenance.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, numerous method and experimental passages, conclusion, limitations, and Appendices A/C undergo extensive rewriting. Section 5.6 reorders its analyses, and author information and acknowledgments change. The language revision is substantial despite the retained overall section structure and core scientific narrative.

P2.justification: v4 redesigns the main comparison table with uncertainty and gain columns and adds Tables 6, 10, and 15. Other tables and Algorithm 1 are relocated or renumbered, and descriptive Table 1 loses its OOS row. These are localized display changes within the retained two-column layout; the three figures remain substantively unchanged.

improvement.justification: v4 improves empirical transparency and support through uncertainty reporting, broader downstream comparisons, direct annotation-agreement evidence, and clearer annotation/access information. It also corrects the role-assignment equation and includes naming in cost accounting. These provide a net quality gain, although undefined significance markers and sparse downstream evaluation details limit the added rigor.
